title: Fix config parsing for offline bundle paths with spaces and Windows separators
author: Jordan Lee
description:
Problem: A few pilot/on-prem customer environments (notably Windows-based jump hosts and shared network mounts) are providing `offline_bundle_path` values that our config loader fails to parse reliably. We saw two recurring failure modes: (1) paths containing spaces (e.g., `D:\Offline Media\Redwood Private\bundle-2026.01.0\`) being split/trimmed incorrectly by our env/config parsing helper, and (2) Windows-style separators/backslashes being interpreted as escape sequences in YAML/JSON-in-YAML contexts or getting double-normalized when combined with URI-ish prefixes (e.g., `file://D:\bundles\...`). The result was a misleading downstream error ("bundle not found" / verification failure) even when the bundle exists and the manifest+signature are valid. This PR hardens config parsing for bundle paths by introducing a single normalization path for filesystem locations, tightening validation and error messages, and expanding test coverage across Linux/macOS/Windows style inputs.

Changes: - Introduce `NormalizeBundlePath()` used by both CLI flag parsing and config file parsing, with explicit handling for: leading/trailing quotes, `file://` and `file:///` prefixes, Windows drive letters, UNC paths (`\\server\share\...`), and mixed separators. - Avoid treating backslashes as escapes by moving YAML string post-processing earlier and preserving raw values when possible; we only normalize separators after decoding has completed. - Add a targeted "did you mean to quote this path?" hint when the input contains spaces and is coming from env var/inline config. - Improve error taxonomy to distinguish: missing path, unreadable directory, missing manifest file, and "path normalized to a different location" (logged at debug). - Keep behavior fail-closed: no fallback to network download and no implicit relative-path resolution in air-gapped mode.

Why in `redwood` repo: While the installer owns preflight verification, the on-prem control plane and some auxiliary tools read the same config and pass bundle locations to the installer and support tooling. Fixing normalization centrally prevents subtle mismatches between components.

Testing: - Unit tests added for normalization across inputs (spaces, quotes, `file://`, drive letters, UNC, mixed separators). - Integration test: run config load + preflight path resolution on a Windows-style path fixture (executed in CI via path simulation; does not require Windows runner). - Manual: verified against a sample bundle staged in a directory with spaces; preflight now resolves correctly and signature verification proceeds.

Notes/Rollout: This is low risk and backwards compatible. The only behavior change is that previously-broken inputs now resolve to the intended directory, and we emit clearer errors when the bundle directory truly cannot be read. This unblocks a subset of air-gapped pilots and reduces support time spent debugging "verification failed" symptoms that are really path parsing.
commits: config: add bundle path normalization helper and call sites
config: improve error messages for invalid/missing bundle paths
tests: add fixtures for Windows/UNC and space-containing paths
docs(dev): note quoting guidance for offline_bundle_path examples
conversation: Ethan Park (review): The normalization helper looks good, but please confirm we are not accidentally accepting relative paths in air-gapped mode. We should keep fail-closed semantics consistent with installer preflight.

Jordan Lee (author): Confirmed. `NormalizeBundlePath()` does not resolve relative paths; it rejects them unless explicitly allowed by the caller. For offline bundle locations we call it with `allowRelative=false` and add a test case for `./bundle` rejection.
Sahana Iyer (review): Can we add coverage for `file:///C:/...`? We see both `file://D:\...` and POSIX-ish file URLs from some packaging scripts.

Jordan Lee (author): Added tests for `file:///C:/bundles/...` and `file:///mnt/offline/bundles/...`. Also tightened the parser to treat `file://D:\...` as a best-effort legacy form (warns in debug, normalizes to `D:\...`).

Marcus Lin (security review): Please make sure we're not doing any silent canonicalization that changes the trust boundary (e.g., stripping `..` segments) in a way that could be exploited to point verification at a different directory. We should either reject or log clearly.

Jordan Lee (author): Good call. We now explicitly reject any path containing `..` segments for offline bundle locations (same as installer behavior), and the error message calls it out. Added unit tests.
Ethan Park (approval): Looks good. Thanks for aligning behavior across config + preflight. Approving.
CI (bot): All checks passed (unit, integration, lint).
Jordan Lee (author): Merging (squash) to unblock next RC. Linked SUP-31844 for tracking.
release_notes: Private/on-prem: Config now correctly parses offline bundle paths containing spaces and Windows-style separators; improved errors when the bundle path is invalid or unreadable.
